title: Timeout fixes must be applied at the effective layer
summary: Changing a timeout option in the nearest request call may not affect the actual deadline. Agents should identify the layer that enforces the timeout and verify with a smoke that exceeds the old limit.
ai_value: Prevents agents from repeatedly patching timeout literals that look plausible but are ignored by the driver, pool, proxy, or platform actually enforcing the deadline.

contexts: database or provider reads fail at a consistent deadline despite local timeout changes
client libraries have both per-request and connection/pool/global timeout options
a query or API call is expected to be slow but safe when bounded by chunking and cancellation rules

trigger_signals.description: Failures still happen at the same fixed duration after a timeout option was changed nearby.
trigger_signals.pattern: timeout after 15s|timeout after 30s|same deadline|requestTimeout|pool timeout|connection timeout
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: The changed option is probably not the enforcing layer.

trigger_signals.description: The client has multiple timeout scopes such as request, pool, connection, statement, socket, proxy, or load balancer.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Map the timeout hierarchy before changing code.

negative_signals.description: The failure duration changes exactly as expected after the local option change and is covered by a regression test or timed smoke.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: The effective layer may already have been identified.

negative_signals.description: The slow operation should be optimized or indexed rather than allowed to run longer.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Timeout extension can hide an algorithmic or data-model problem.

common_wrong_assumptions: The timeout option closest to the query is always the one being enforced.
A code diff that increases a timeout proves the runtime deadline changed.
A successful fast query validates a timeout fix.

first_checks.check: Create a timeout map naming every layer that can cancel the call and its current configured deadline.
first_checks.why: The actual deadline is the earliest active cancellation source.

first_checks.check: Run a bounded smoke that is expected to take longer than the old deadline and shorter than the new one, then record measured duration and success/failure.
first_checks.why: Only a >old-timeout smoke proves the effective deadline moved.
files: reviewed test query or API call

decision_rules.condition: A timeout remains fixed after local option changes or the client exposes pool/global timeout settings.
decision_rules.then: Change the enforcing layer, keep the operation bounded, and verify with a timed smoke that crosses the former deadline.

do_not: Do not claim a timeout fix from a fast-path smoke that completes below the old deadline.
Do not increase timeouts to mask an unbounded query, missing index, or runaway batch without a separate design check.
Do not publish private driver configs, hostnames, tenant identifiers, SQL text containing business data, or internal paths in public lessons.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: When a timeout patch seems ignored, map cancellation layers and verify the selected layer with a timed smoke exceeding the former limit.

risk.notes: Candidate is based on a private production-backed import; timed smokes against live systems require normal production/data gates.

sources.supports: A database import continued to hit the old deadline until the timeout was moved from per-request code to the client pool configuration and verified with a query exceeding the former limit.
